title: Introduction to Vishnu in 10 Minutes
notes: Each shot has narration lines. '|' splits a line into on-screen caption beats, *word* marks the highlighted word.

shots.v: A moonlit cosmic ocean, slow waves, stars reflected in the water.
lines: Imagine an ocean with no shore, | no beginning, | and no *end.*

shots.v: The many-hooded serpent Shesha rises from the waves; Vishnu rests on its coils in silhouette, then glows.
lines: On its gentle waves floats a great serpent, | with a thousand *heads.*
And resting upon it, | calm as the deep sea, | is the one who holds the universe *together.*

shots.v: Vishnu revealed in full colour with conch, chakra, mace and lotus. Title card.
lines: This is *Vishnu* —| the preserver, the *protector.*
He is one of the most beloved gods in Hinduism, | worshipped by hundreds of millions | around the *world.*
In the next ten minutes, | let us get to *know* him.

shots.v: Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu side by side; each lights up in turn.
lines: In Hindu tradition, | three great gods | care for the *universe.*
Brahma *creates* it.
Shiva *transforms* it.
And Vishnu *preserves* it.

shots.v: A golden scale balances a glowing world; Vishnu's hand steadies it.
lines: Brahma begins each world, | and Shiva brings it to a close. | But through all the long ages in between, | it is Vishnu who watches over *life.*
His task is to keep the world in *balance* —| to protect what is good, | and to guard *dharma,* | the way of truth and *kindness.*

shots.v: Vishnu's outline filled with stars, rivers and hearts; then a warm portrait.
lines: His name means the one who is *everywhere* —| in every star, every river, | and every living *heart.*
He is also called *Narayana,* | the shelter of all *beings.*
And to his devotees, | he is the Supreme himself, | the source of *everything.*

shots.v: Full four-armed figure of Vishnu against a sunburst.
lines: Look closely at Vishnu, | for everything about him | has a *meaning.*

shots.v: Close on his serene blue face; sky and ocean blend behind him.
lines: His skin is the deep blue | of the sky and the *ocean* —| vast, calm, and without *limit.*

shots.v: The four arms open outward, each trailing light to a corner of the frame.
lines: He has four *arms,* | reaching out in every direction, | to care for the whole *world.*

shots.v: Hero shot of the white conch; rings of sound and a glowing Om.
lines: In one hand is the *conch,* | the shankha.
Its deep note is the first sound of creation —| the sacred *Om.*

shots.v: The Sudarshana chakra spins, throwing sparks and slicing through dark clouds.
lines: In another spins the *chakra,* | a blazing wheel called Sudarshana —| which cuts through darkness | and *evil.*

shots.v: The golden mace gleams against a royal crimson sunburst.
lines: The third holds a golden *mace,* | a sign of strength, | and the power of *knowledge.*

shots.v: A lotus rises from a dark pond and opens in light.
lines: And the fourth holds a *lotus* —| a flower that rises pure and bright, | even from muddy *water.*

shots.v: Camera travels over yellow garments, flower garland and the jewel on his chest.
lines: He wears garments of golden *yellow,* | a garland of forest flowers, | and on his chest, a shining *jewel.*
On his head is a tall golden *crown,* | for he is the king and guardian | of all the *worlds.*

shots.v: Golden gates and domes above the clouds, radiant sky.
lines: Vishnu's home is *Vaikuntha* —| a realm of light, | where there is no sorrow | and no *fear.*

shots.v: Lakshmi on a pink lotus showering golden coins; then Vishnu and Lakshmi together.
lines: Beside him is the goddess *Lakshmi,* | giver of fortune, beauty, and *grace.*
Wherever Vishnu goes, | she goes with him —| for protection and prosperity | belong *together.*

shots.v: Vishnu reclines on Shesha's coils under the canopy of hoods; Lakshmi at his feet.
lines: His bed is the serpent *Shesha,* | whose name means | that which *remains* —| when everything else is *gone.*

shots.v: Garuda, the golden eagle, soars through clouds with Vishnu on his back.
lines: And when he travels, | he rides *Garuda,* | the mighty king of birds, | swifter than the *wind.*

shots.v: A lotus stem rises from the resting Vishnu; Brahma sits in the bloom and worlds appear.
lines: They say that from Vishnu's navel | grew a single *lotus,* | and from that lotus | Brahma was born, | to create the *worlds.*

shots.v: The balanced scale tips; storm clouds swallow a bright village.
lines: But sometimes, | the world loses its *balance.*
Cruelty grows strong, | and goodness is in *danger.*

shots.v: Vishnu rises, hand lifted in blessing; a beam of light descends through the clouds.
lines: For those times, | Vishnu made a *promise.*
Whenever dharma fades, | and darkness rises, | I will come *down* —| age after *age.*

shots.v: Ten glowing medallions appear in an arc around Vishnu.
lines: Each time he comes, | he takes a new *form.*
These are his *avatars.* | The ten most famous | are called the *Dashavatara.*

shots.v: Matsya, the golden fish, tows a small boat through towering waves.
lines: First came *Matsya,* the fish, | who guided a boat of life | safely through a great *flood.*
He saved the wise king Manu, | the seeds of every plant, | and the sacred *Vedas.*

shots.v: Kurma the tortoise beneath a mountain wrapped by a serpent rope.
lines: Then *Kurma,* the tortoise, | who carried a mountain on his back, | as gods and demons churned the *ocean.*

shots.v: Varaha the boar rises from dark water lifting the Earth on his tusks.
lines: As *Varaha,* the mighty boar, | he dived into the deep, | and lifted the Earth | back into the *light.*

shots.v: A palace pillar splits; Narasimha roars out as little Prahlada prays.
lines: As *Narasimha,* half man, half lion, | he burst from a pillar | to save a child named *Prahlada* | from a cruel *king.*

shots.v: Small Vamana with umbrella; then a giant foot covering the Earth.
lines: As *Vamana,* a small boy, | he asked a proud king for just three steps of *land* —| then grew so vast | that he covered earth and sky | in *two.*

shots.v: Parashurama the warrior sage with his axe on a mountain ridge.
lines: As *Parashurama,* the warrior sage, | he humbled rulers | who had forgotten *justice.*

shots.v: Rama with his bow before a golden city; Sita joins him.
lines: As *Rama,* prince of Ayodhya, | he showed what it means to be *good* —| a loyal son, a faithful husband, | and a just *king.*
His story, the *Ramayana,* | tells how he crossed the sea | to rescue his wife Sita | from the demon king *Ravana.*

shots.v: Krishna plays the flute under a full moon; cows and peacock feathers; then the chariot.
lines: As *Krishna,* | he played his flute, | danced with his friends, | and taught the wisdom | of the Bhagavad *Gita.*
On a great battlefield, | he told the warrior Arjuna: | do what is right, | and let go of the *reward.*

shots.v: The Buddha meditating beneath the Bodhi tree, soft dawn light.
lines: In many traditions, | the ninth is the *Buddha,* | teacher of compassion and *peace.*
Some traditions name Krishna's brother, | *Balarama,* instead.

shots.v: Kalki on a white horse, sword raised, against a comet-streaked sky.
lines: And the tenth, *Kalki,* | is yet to *come* —| riding a white horse, | at the end of this *age.*

shots.v: All ten avatar medallions circle Vishnu.
lines: Ten forms. | One *purpose.* | To protect the good, | and bring the world back into *balance.*
From fish, to beast, to human —| some see in these ten forms | the long story of life *itself.*

shots.v: A lotus lake; the elephant king is caught by a crocodile.
lines: One story shows his heart | better than any *other.*
An elephant king named *Gajendra* | was seized by a crocodile, | and no one could set him *free.*

shots.v: The elephant lifts a lotus in his trunk toward the sky.
lines: With his last strength, | he lifted a lotus to the sky, | and called out to *Vishnu.*

shots.v: Vishnu dives on Garuda; the chakra flashes across the lake.
lines: At once, Vishnu came flying on Garuda —| and with his spinning chakra, | he *saved* him.

shots.v: A small prince meditates in a forest; Vishnu appears and lifts him into the sky as the Pole Star.
lines: Another story tells of a little prince named *Dhruva,* | who prayed to Vishnu | with all his *heart.*
Vishnu was so moved | that he made him the *Pole Star* —| steady and bright, | for all of *time.*

shots.v: Vishnu blesses the bowing elephant; lotus petals fall.
lines: Vishnu does not ask who you *are.*
He comes to anyone | who calls with a sincere *heart.*

shots.v: Names drift like lanterns; three portraits: Hari, Govinda, Jagannath.
lines: Vishnu has a thousand *names.*
*Hari,* | the one who takes away *sorrow.*
*Govinda,* | the friend of the *gentle.*
*Jagannath,* | the lord of the *universe.*

shots.v: A stylised map of India; three temples light up south, north and east.
lines: Great temples rise in his honour —| Tirupati in the south, | Badrinath in the Himalayas, | and Puri by the *sea.*

shots.v: A devotee offers tulsi leaves at a shrine; singers with raised hands and lamps.
lines: His followers are called *Vaishnavas,* | and theirs is one of the largest traditions | in all of *Hinduism.*
His devotees offer leaves of *tulsi,* | the holy basil he *loves.*
They fast on the day of *Ekadashi,* | and they sing his names with *joy.*
Festivals like *Diwali,* | Janmashtami, | and Rama Navami | all celebrate his *avatars.*

shots.v: A glowing Om; the eight syllables of the mantra light one by one.
lines: And on their lips is one mantra: | *Om Namo Narayanaya.*
I bow to the one | who lives in *all.*

shots.v: Montage: the calm ocean, the protector with chakra, the avatars returning.
lines: So, who is Vishnu?
He is the calm | of the deep *ocean.*
The protector, | who never looks *away.*
The friend | who returns, again and again, | whenever he is *needed.*

shots.v: Serene Vishnu at sunrise; three soft symbols appear.
lines: He teaches that goodness | is worth *protecting,*
that power should always | serve *kindness,*
and that no one who asks for help | is ever truly *alone.*

shots.v: A child shelters a small bird; a faint blue glow of Vishnu stands behind.
lines: So whenever you protect something good —| a friend, a promise, a living *thing* —| a little of Vishnu's work | is done through *you.*

shots.v: Vishnu and Lakshmi in full glory; end title.
lines: Om Namo *Narayanaya.*
